characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective of 221B Baker Street; master of disguise (appears as a drunken groom, a Nonconformist clergyman).

characters.name: Dr. John Watson
characters.note: Holmes's friend, chronicler and accomplice; married, in medical practice.

characters.name: Irene Adler
characters.note: American contralto and adventuress of New Jersey; holds the compromising photograph.

characters.name: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, King of Bohemia
characters.note: Appears masked and disguised; heir to the House of Ormstein.

characters.name: Godfrey Norton
aliases: Mr. Norton of the Inner Temple
characters.note: Dark, handsome lawyer; Irene Adler's suitor and bridegroom.

characters.name: clergyman of St. Monica's
characters.note: Unnamed priest who marries Norton and Adler, insisting on a witness.

characters.name: Violet Hunter
characters.note: Governess with chestnut hair, client of the Copper Beeches case.

characters.name: Jephro Rucastle
characters.note: Stout, smiling Hampshire gentleman; imprisons his daughter.

characters.name: Mrs. Rucastle
characters.note: Silent, pale-faced second wife, devoted to husband and son.

characters.name: Edward Rucastle
characters.note: The Rucastles' spoiled, cruel six-year-old son.

characters.name: Alice Rucastle
characters.note: Rucastle's daughter by his first marriage; never on stage, only discussed.

characters.name: Toller
characters.note: Drunken groom, sole handler of the mastiff.

characters.name: Mrs. Toller
characters.note: Tall, sour-faced servant who knows the household's secret.

characters.name: Mr. Fowler
aliases: the man in the grey suit
the bearded man on the road
characters.note: Persevering seaman who rescues Alice; never on stage directly.

characters.name: Miss Stoper
characters.note: Runs the governess agency; appears only in Violet Hunter's retelling.

characters.name: Carlo
characters.note: Huge tawny mastiff kept starved and loosed at night; an animal that acts.

characters.name: Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen
characters.note: The King's betrothed; named only, never on stage.

characters.name: Mrs. Turner
characters.note: Baker Street landlady in this story; mentioned, briefly serving.

locations.name: 221B Baker Street
locations.note: Holmes's sitting-room and bedroom, with fireplace, gas, seventeen stairs.

locations.name: Briony Lodge
locations.note: Irene Adler's bijou villa with garden, coach-house and mews lane.

locations.name: Church of St. Monica
locations.note: Where Norton and Adler marry in haste.

locations.name: The Copper Beeches
locations.note: Whitewashed square house near Winchester, woods on three sides, copper beeches at the door, mastiff kennel, locked wing.

locations.name: The Black Swan Hotel
locations.note: Inn in Winchester where Holmes and Watson meet Violet Hunter.

locations.name: Westaway's governess agency
locations.note: West End employment office; appears in Violet's retelling.

brief.era: Late Victorian London, 1888–early 1890s; gaslight, fog, hansom cabs and broughams.
brief.place: Holmes's sitting-room at 221B Baker Street (cheery fire, gas lamps, cluttered shelves, cigars and spirit case); a St. John's Wood villa; a small church; a Hampshire country house with copper beeches; a Winchester inn.
brief.dress: Men in frock coats, top hats, ulsters; Watson in dark suits with medical touches. Holmes in disguise: shabby groom, benevolent Nonconformist clergyman with broad black hat and white tie. The King of Bohemia in barbaric opulence: astrakhan-trimmed coat, flame-lined blue cloak, flaming beryl brooch, fur-topped boots, black vizard mask. Irene Adler elegant and lovely. Violet Hunter plainly, neatly dressed; her chestnut hair later cut short; an electric-blue dress worn indoors. Jephro Rucastle prodigiously stout, smiling, small eyes.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Briony Lodge: bijou villa, long ground-floor windows, Chubb lock, coach-house. Copper Beeches: whitewashed square block, clump of copper beeches, shuttered window, padlocked door barred with an iron bedstead, skylight, light ladder, kennel with chained mastiff, wine-cellar.
depiction_rules: Holmes's disguises must be shown as convincing: other characters do not recognise him.
The King wears his mask until he tears it off; before that, only the lower face visible.
Carlo the mastiff is a huge, starved, tawny dog with black muzzle, shown as a menacing animal, never anthropomorphised.
Alice Rucastle and Mr. Fowler never appear on stage; do not depict them except as distant figures (the man in the grey suit on the road).
The fire at Briony Lodge is a trick: smoke-rocket and crowd cries, no real blaze.
